headline: Fix first. The database and RLS hold under every attack QA ran, and sign-in, sign out and sign out everywhere work end to end. But four Majors stand: no test pins production's random codes, pgTAP can't see a weak UPDATE WITH CHECK, a signed-in person opening Sen offline lands on sign-in, and three wrong codes lock a person into a 'send a new code' loop. Malformed JSON also gets a 500 where it should get a 400.

suites.e2e: 1387 specs, 1386 pass; the 1 failure (redesign-pins tap guard) passed 5/5 alone, so it's flaky under load, not a B05 regression
suites.diff: 1 screen changed (settings/account, as asked), 0 check findings

findings.title: Nothing tests that production refuses the fixed preview code 123456
findings.detail: `createAuth` fixes every code to `123456` unless `target === 'production'` (`apps/api/src/auth.ts`). The API tests run with `target: 'production'` but their mailer records whatever code is sent, so a production server that always sends `123456` passes every test. This is the one line between a public repo's documented code and the owner's real account. The code is right today (QA sent three production codes: 221323, 800570, 937721), but nothing would notice a regression.
findings.repro: sed -i "s/const fixedCode = opts.target !== 'production';/const fixedCode = true;/" apps/api/src/auth.ts && pnpm test:db; git checkout -- apps/api/src/auth.ts

findings.title: pgTAP can’t see a weak WITH CHECK on UPDATE: the harness every later table relies on misses it
findings.detail: rls.sql's *can't give its own row to someone else* runs `UPDATE t SET user_id = C WHERE user_id = me`. Because the WHERE names a column, Postgres also applies the SELECT policy to the new row, which refuses it, so the test says `denied` even when the UPDATE policy's WITH CHECK is wrong. With `WITH CHECK (user_id is not null)` the suite stays green, while `UPDATE user_settings SET user_id = C` (no WHERE on the column) as B moves B's row into C's account. The brief makes this harness the proof for every later table, so a later table with a weak WITH CHECK would pass.
findings.repro: In packages/db/migrations/0001_b05_tables.sql change user_settings_own_update's WITH CHECK to ("user_settings"."user_id" is not null); pnpm test:db (stays green). Then in a database with that policy: set role app_user; select set_config('app.user_id', B, true); update user_settings set user_id = C;

findings.title: Signed in but offline, opening Sen lands on sign-in
findings.detail: The signed-out gate (`router.tsx` beforeLoad) asks `auth.session()`, which turns any failed `/api/auth/get-session` into `null`. Offline, with the service worker serving the app, a signed-in person opening `/review` is sent to `sign-in`, which then says signing in needs a connection. On `main` the app opened offline. flows.md *offline*: Review, manual entry and scanning still work offline; §5.1: the app opens offline. Back online, the person is still parked on `/s/sign-in` (an open route), though signed in. Two offline banners stack on that screen.
findings.repro: qa/e2e: ./node_modules/.bin/playwright test -c b05.config.ts b05-offline (sign in, let the service worker control the page, setOffline(true), goto /review)

FLOW-10c: offline open lands on: http://localhost:4177/s/sign-in | You're offline. What you add is kept and syncs when you're back. | Sen | Sen | You’re offline. Signing in needs a connection. | Sign in to Sen | …

findings.title: After three wrong codes, *Send a new code* sends one that is refused with the same message
findings.detail: Better Auth rate-limits `/sign-in/email-otp` to 3 calls a minute per client, and `auth.ts` (web) maps any 429 to `too-many`, shown as *That code has had too many tries. Send a new code.* So two typos and the right code works, but three typos lock the person out for a minute: the right code is refused, *Send a new code* sends a new one (toast), and that new code is refused with the same instruction to send a new code. Each send also spends the 3-a-minute send limit. Nothing says to wait.
findings.repro: Sign in as qa-chong: Send the code; type 111111, 222222, 333333, then 123456; Send a new code; type 123456 at once. (qa/e2e b05-flows FLOW-4)

FLOW-4: the NEW code, typed at once, says: "That code has had too many tries. Send a new code."; url http://localhost:4177/s/sign-in; sessions 0
curl, one IP: INVALID_OTP 400 ×3, then 429; send 200; sign-in with the new code: {"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."} 429
auth_rate_limit: 10.44.44.44|/sign-in/email-otp|3
findings.spec: AC-42, screens.md sign-in, flows.md first-run (Wrong or expired code: Send a new code)

findings.title: Malformed JSON, an empty body and an empty PATCH answer 500
findings.detail: `c.req.json()` throws a SyntaxError that `onError` turns into a 500 `{code:'server'}` on `/api/commands` and on every resource route; `PATCH /:id` with `{}` on a table without `updated_at` reaches Drizzle's *No values to set*, also a 500. The shape holds and no stack leaks, but spec §16 and QA's rule want a 400 for bad input, never a 500, and a 500 hides the client's mistake in the server's error count.
findings.repro: curl -X POST localhost:8790/api/commands -H 'content-type: application/json' -b <session> --data-binary 'not json'   (and with an empty body)

findings.title: Code sends are limited per client IP only; the 429 has no code; invitation lookups are unthrottled
findings.detail: The handoff's *3 codes a minute per address* is per client IP (Better Auth's rate limit), not per email: from rotating addresses QA sent 12 codes to weiming@example.com on the live preview inside a minute, all 200. In production each is a Gmail send, so anyone can spend Sen's Gmail quota and bury the owner's real code. The 429 body is `{"message":…}` without `code`. The invitation-only check runs before the limiter, so `not_invited` answers are unlimited (10 of 10 from one IP), an open membership oracle. Locally, behind Vite's proxy, Better Auth logs that it can't find the client IP and falls back to one shared bucket.

preview, rotating egress IPs: 200 200 200 200 200 / 200 200 200 200 200 / 200 200
local, one IP: 200 200 200 429 429; body {"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}
stranger lookups, one IP: 403 ×10
WARN [Better Auth]: Rate limiting could not determine a client IP and is falling back to a single shared per-path bucket.

findings.title: A retried write adds an audit row and moves updated_at
findings.detail: `setting.set` and the resource `PUT` have no dedupe: the same command twice writes a second audit row with identical before and after, and bumps `updated_at`. The state is right, but the log records a change that didn't happen, and a later *Undo* reads it.
findings.evidence: audit rows before=4 after two identical commands=6; updated_at 2026-10-15 17:54:26.379967+00 -> 2026-10-15 17:54:26.485787+00
findings.spec: AC-23, CLAUDE.md *Every input has a dedupe key*

findings.title: /api/admin/members returns the raw switches, not MemberRow’s seven
findings.detail: `switches: m.features` passes the jsonb through, so a person whose row holds `{"capture":true}` comes back with one key, where `@sen/core/views` MemberRow requires all seven booleans. `/api/settings` merges with NO_SWITCHES; this route doesn't. B38's screens will parse it.

findings.title: Sign-in and Account drift from patterns.md
findings.detail: Account: the Email row is information but leads with an icon tile (patterns §7: *a row that opens nothing is information and has no tile*); *Sign out* and *Sign out everywhere* are actions drawn as NavRows with chevrons, so they look like destinations (*information and actions never look alike*). Sign-in: *Send the code* and *Sign in* are disabled offline (§7 Forms: *the submit button stays enabled and says what's missing*), and offline the screen stacks two banners that say different things. The dialog's cancel reads *Keep it*.
findings.repro: Open Settings → Account; go offline on sign-in.

FLOW-10c screen: two banners, “You're offline. What you add is kept and syncs when you're back.” and “You’re offline. Signing in needs a connection.”

findings.title: A suspended person signs in and nothing says so
findings.detail: The API refuses a suspended person with 403 `suspended` on every route, but sign-in still succeeds and the app shows its screens (in a preview, Wei Ming's made-up month) without a word. §9.6: *Suspend (signs them out everywhere)*. The screens are B38's, but the API's refusal is B05's and the web app ignores it.

findings.evidence: FLOW-15: suspended, after sign-in: http://localhost:4177/ | Sen | Sen | Home | Payday plan · 2 of 3 | Left until payday | RM | 1,931.27 …

findings.title: Audit before/after use Drizzle’s camelCase keys
findings.detail: The writer stores the Drizzle row (`expectedPayday`, `ownNames`, `updatedAt`), while pgTAP's fixture and SQL readers would expect column names (`expected_payday`). Settle one before the agent and Undo read audit_log.
findings.repro: select before from audit_log order by created_at desc limit 1

findings.title: Every signed-out load calls /api/me and logs a 401
findings.detail: The sign-in screen's frame asks `/api/me`, which answers 401 and logs a console error on every signed-out visit.

findings.title: Any preview’s admin is one public email and code away
findings.detail: Previews seed Wei Ming as the admin with a fixed code, and both are in the public repo, so anyone can sign in to any preview as its admin and write to the shared sen-preview database. The data is made up, so it's accepted; it does mean a preview's state can't be trusted between QA runs.

findings.title: Emails are compared case-sensitively in the database
findings.detail: `invitations_open_email_key` and `auth_user_email_unique` are plain unique indexes: `PEND@example.com` was accepted as a second pending invitation beside `pend@example.com`. The API lowercases before it looks up; B38's invitation writer must too, or the indexes should be on lower(email).
findings.repro: insert two pending invitations differing only in case

findings.title: The function’s runtime holds the owner role’s URL
findings.detail: `readEnv` derives the roles' URLs from `DATABASE_URL`, the Neon integration's owner URL, so the API function's environment holds the owner's credentials at runtime, though it never connects with them. §17 says only migrations and the backup use the owner role; a function compromise would reach it. A host-only variable would keep it out.

findings.title: Switch names differ from the spec
findings.detail: `features` holds `email` where §15 says `email_receipts`, and the column has no check on its keys.
